note: Curated source-linked Sunday scan. Headlines remain attributable to the originating publishers; this is discovery material, not a numbered East Corner editorial conclusion.

items.sourceHeadline: Tanzania commissions country's largest hydropower plant
items.sourceDescription: Tanzania commissioned a 2,115-megawatt hydropower plant, more than doubling national generation capacity and creating potential room for power exports and additional industrial demand.

items.sourceHeadline: Official creditors back Ethiopia bond restructuring, flag risks in warrant
items.sourceDescription: Ethiopia's official creditors approved a preliminary restructuring agreement covering the country's $1 billion Eurobond, moving the sovereign closer to an exit from default while creditors continue to scrutinize the proposed terms.

items.sourceHeadline: Somali child hunger crisis deepens as facilities close due to aid cuts, UNICEF says
items.sourceDescription: UNICEF said 205 health and nutrition facilities have closed after humanitarian funding cuts, while nearly 1.9 million Somali children are projected to experience malnutrition in 2026.

items.sourceHeadline: Uganda eyes up to $242 million from Citibank for infrastructure project
items.sourceDescription: Uganda is considering borrowing up to 207.7 million euros from Citibank to help finance a major road project in the country's east, linking commercial bank financing directly to public infrastructure delivery.

items.sourceHeadline: Kenya Airways says its fuel cost up 72% due to Middle East conflict
items.sourceDescription: Kenya Airways said Middle East conflict lifted first-half fuel costs by 72% and disrupted spare-parts supply and aircraft maintenance, transmitting geopolitical pressure directly into regional aviation operating costs.

items.sourceHeadline: Kenya's competition regulator seeks reserve fund in Diageo's EABL sale
items.sourceDescription: Kenya's competition regulator proposed a reserve of up to 15 billion shillings before approving the sale of Diageo's EABL stake to Asahi, placing regulatory risk allocation directly inside a major cross-border transaction.
